answer: Each VDF output is verified against the epoch seed, and the proof size stays small. Parallel machines cannot shorten a sequential delay, so 158 aliases need 158 separate VDF evaluations. A Wesolowski VDF proves sequential work in an RSA group, and the proof verifies in milliseconds. Watch the mirror: the farm pays per alias, the honest agent pays once, the reef bond is locked until the epoch ends, and the kernel audit is open to anyone who wants to re-run it.
